items.t: Said St. Louis needs to reduce crime and that improving schools statewide should start in St. Louis.
items.q: St. Louis needs to clean up its act in many ways. It starts with reducing crime. We are also working to improve our schools statewide and there’s no better place to start than in St. Louis.

record.t: Was elected Senate majority floor leader of the Missouri Senate for the 102nd General Assembly, the first female to hold that office in the chamber's history.
record.q: The Missouri Senate Majority Caucus elected Sen. Cindy O’Laughlin, R-Shelbina, to serve as the Senate majority floor leader for the 102nd General Assembly, the first female to hold this office in the Missouri Senate’s history.

record.t: Was elected Missouri Senate president pro tem, the first woman to hold that post.
record.q: On Wednesday, Jan. 8, Sen. Cindy O'Laughlin, R-Shelbina, made history by becoming the first female to be elected Missouri Senate president pro tem.

record.t: Served as chairwoman of the Senate Education Committee.
record.q: state Sen. Cindy O'Laughlin, R-Shelbina, chairwoman of the Senate Education Committee, recently told the Springfield News-Leader.

record.t: Discussed Senate Bills 4, 42 and 89, which seek to modify provisions regarding elementary and secondary education and have received preliminary Senate approval.
record.q: Senator Cindy O’Laughlin discusses Senate Bills 4, 42 & 89, legislation that seeks to modify provisions regarding elementary and secondary education.
